Fix an arm \(a\), an atom \(s\in S_a\), a cell \(e\in E\) with \(e_a=s\), and put
\[
 w=\sum_{b\ne a}z_{be_b},\qquad g=-2w.
\]
By the definition of \(G_{as}\), every member of \(G_{as}\) arises in this way from some such support cell.  Dual feasibility and tightness on \(E\), as recorded in the definition of \(u_{as}\), give
\[
 u_{as}+\sum_{b\ne a}u_{be_b}=(z_{as}+w)^2
\]
and, after replacing only coordinate \(a\) by an arbitrary \(t\in S_a\),
\[
 u_{at}+\sum_{b\ne a}u_{be_b}\le (z_{at}+w)^2.
\]
Subtracting the first display from the second and using \(\phi_{ar}=z_{ar}^2-u_{ar}\) yields
\[
 \phi_{at}-\phi_{as}
 \ge -2w(z_{at}-z_{as})
 =g(z_{at}-z_{as}). \tag{1}
\]
This proves the first assertion for every \(g\in G_{as}\).  Each distinct marginal atom has positive multiplicity; because \(q^\star\) has that marginal, the atom is incident to a cell of its positive support \(E\).  Thus every \(G_{as}\) is nonempty.

Suppose \(z_{as}<z_{at}\) and set \(d=z_{at}-z_{as}>0\).  Apply (1) first from \(s\) to \(t\), and then from \(t\) to \(s\).  For every \(g\in G_{as}\) and \(h\in G_{at}\), this gives
\[
 gd\le \phi_{at}-\phi_{as}\le hd,
 \qquad
 g\le \frac{\phi_{at}-\phi_{as}}{z_{at}-z_{as}}\le h. \tag{2}
\]
In particular, \(\max G_{as}\le\min G_{at}\), and therefore
\[
 z_{as}+\max G_{as}<z_{at}+\min G_{at}. \tag{3}
\]
Thus the closed intervals \(I_{as}\) are strictly ordered by \(z_{as}\) and are pairwise disjoint within each arm.  The fixed contrast and the support \([0,1]\) give
\[
 z_1,z_2\in[0,1/4],\qquad z_3\in[-1/2,0].
\]
For \(a=1\) or \(a=2\), the sum of the other two coordinates belongs to \([-1/2,1/4]\), whereas for \(a=3\) it belongs to \([0,1/2]\).  Consequently
\[
 G_{1s},G_{2s}\subset[-1/2,1],\qquad G_{3s}\subset[-1,0],
\]
and hence
\[
 I_{1s},I_{2s}\subset[-1/2,5/4],\qquad
 I_{3s}\subset[-3/2,0]. \tag{4}
\]

Finally, suppose that \(I_{as}\) and \(I_{at}\) are contained in a common interval \(J\) of length \(H\).  If \(s=t\), both claimed quantities vanish.  If \(z_{as}<z_{at}\), choose \(g\in G_{as}\) and \(h\in G_{at}\).  By (2), \(h-g\ge0\), while the two points \(z_{as}+g,z_{at}+h\in J\) obey
\[
 (z_{at}-z_{as})+(h-g)
 =(z_{at}+h)-(z_{as}+g)\le H. \tag{5}
\]
Both nonnegative summands in (5) are at most \(H\).  If \(m=[\phi_{at}-\phi_{as}]/[z_{at}-z_{as}]\), then (2) gives \(g\le m\le h\), and therefore
\[
 |z_{at}-z_{as}|\le H,\quad
 0\le \phi_{at}-\phi_{as}-g(z_{at}-z_{as})
 =(m-g)(z_{at}-z_{as})
 \le H^2. \tag{6}
\]
If \(z_{at}<z_{as}\), reverse the order.  Then, for \(h\in G_{at}\), the corresponding secant slope satisfies \(h\le m\le g\), and the remainder is \((g-m)(z_{as}-z_{at})\); the analogue of (5) again bounds both factors by \(H\).  Aggregating repeated observations leaves one atom and positive multiplicity, so it does not alter the argument.  A contact with a grid boundary changes only whether the algorithm declares an interval singleton; (1)--(6) are closed inequalities and remain valid.  This proves the lemma.

For arms \(1,2\), put \(J_a=[-1/2,5/4]\) and \(H_a=7/4\); put \(J_3=[-3/2,0]\) and \(H_3=3/2\).  At depth \(\ell\), Definition def:rounding-algorithm divides \(J_a\) into \(D_\ell=2^\ell\) consecutive cells of width
\[
 h_{a,\ell}=H_a2^{-\ell}, \tag{7}
\]
where all cells are left-closed and right-open except for the right-closed last cell.  By Lemma lem:ordered-dual-slopes, the intervals \(I_{as}\) are strictly disjoint and all lie in \(J_a\).

There is at most one nonsingleton cluster for each of the \(D_\ell\) grid cells.  An interval not contained in one cell is made a singleton.  Such an interval contains at least one of the \(D_\ell-1\) interior boundaries; assign it its leftmost such boundary.  Two strictly disjoint closed intervals cannot be assigned the same boundary.  Hence the assignment is injective and, writing \(K_{a,\ell}=|\mathcal P_{a,\ell}|\),
\[
 K_{a,\ell}
 \le D_\ell+(D_\ell-1)
 =2D_\ell-1. \tag{8}
\]
The right-closed convention places the right endpoint of \(J_a\) in the root grid and prevents an endpoint exception.  It can only turn a boundary-touching interval into a singleton, which is already counted in (8).

The partitions are nested.  Indeed, an interval crossing a coarse boundary also crosses that boundary at every finer depth and stays singleton.  Otherwise, atoms grouped in one fine cell have their intervals in its unique coarse parent cell.  At depth zero the sole cell is the right-closed root \(J_a\); (4) in Lemma lem:ordered-dual-slopes therefore gives \(K_{a,0}=1\).  After repeated observations have been aggregated, distinct atoms in an arm have distinct \(z\)-coordinates because every \(c_a\) is nonzero.  Since there are finitely many atoms, their minimum positive separation is positive.  Choose a common finite \(L\) such that every \(h_{a,L}\) is smaller than that separation in arm \(a\).  If two distinct atoms belonged to one nonsingleton block at depth \(L\), the final assertion of Lemma lem:ordered-dual-slopes would give \(|z_{at}-z_{as}|\le h_{a,L}\), a contradiction.  Thus every depth-\(L\) partition is the singleton partition.

We next prove the residual bound from the integer margins.  At a fixed depth, let \(A_\ell\) be the zero--one incidence matrix whose rows are the clusters in the three partitions and whose columns are the currently available cells of the original support \(E\).  The current residual table is a nonnegative rational solution of
\[
 A_\ell q=b_\ell, \tag{9}
\]
where \(b_\ell\) is the integer vector of original cluster multiplicities minus already frozen integer counts.  If the positive columns in (9) are linearly dependent, choose a nonzero rational vector \(d\), supported on them, with \(A_\ell d=0\).  Summing the cluster rows for any one arm gives the all-ones row on the columns, so \(\sum_e d_e=0\); hence \(d\) has both signs.  With
\[
 \varepsilon=\min_{e:d_e>0}\frac{q_e}{d_e},
\]
the table \(q-\varepsilon d\) remains feasible and nonnegative and has strictly smaller positive support.  Repetition terminates at a table whose positive columns are linearly independent.

The sums of the row blocks belonging to the three arms are equal, giving two independent row relations.  Thus the terminal positive support has size at most
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(A_\ell)\le\sum_{a=1}^3K_{a,\ell}-2. \tag{10}
\]
Freeze \(\lfloor q_e\rfloor\) copies of every positive cell.  Every remaining entry lies in \([0,1)\), and its total \(R_\ell\) is an integer because it equals the sum of the remaining integer cluster margins for any arm.  If the remaining total is positive, (10) and integrality give
\[
 R_\ell<\#\{e:q_e>0\}
 \le\sum_aK_{a,\ell}-2,
 \qquad
 R_\ell\le\sum_aK_{a,\ell}-3. \tag{11}
\]
The same last inequality is immediate when the residual is zero.  At the root, (8) gives three cluster rows and rank one, so the basic table has at most one positive cell.  Its mass is the integer residual total and is completely frozen; hence \(R_0=0\).  For every \(\ell\ge0\), applying (8) and (11) at depth \(\ell+1\) yields
\[
 R_{\ell+1}
 \le\sum_aK_{a,\ell+1}-3
 \le3(2D_{\ell+1}-1)-3
 =6D_{\ell+1}-6
 =12\,2^\ell-6. \tag{12}
\]
Because the root residual is zero, all residual mass has eventually been frozen, and the frozen multiset contains exactly \(N\) cells of \(E\).

It remains to repair the atom multiplicities.  Independently for an arm \(a\), match equal selected and required atoms at the leaves.  At every parent block, match unmatched selected occurrences from its children to unmatched required occurrences from its children and pass the remaining signed imbalance upward.  Equality of the root totals makes the final matching a bijection.  Fix a nonterminal depth \(\ell\), and consider the depth-\(\ell+1\) blocks immediately after freezing at that depth.  For such a block \(B\), let \(f_B\) be the number frozen so far, \(r_B\) its residual fractional margin, and \(l_B\) the number of occurrences selected in \(B\) at all later, coarser freezes.  Feasibility at depth \(\ell+1\) and the construction give
\[
 \operatorname{original}(B)=f_B+r_B,\quad
 \operatorname{selected}(B)=f_B+l_B,\quad
 \sum_Br_B=\sum_Bl_B=R_{\ell+1}. \tag{13}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \frac12\sum_B|\operatorname{selected}(B)-\operatorname{original}(B)|
 =\frac12\sum_B|l_B-r_B|
 \le R_{\ell+1}. \tag{14}
\]
After all matches internal to the depth-\(\ell+1\) blocks, the unmatched occurrences are precisely the signed discrepancies in (14).  Each match whose lowest common partition block has depth \(\ell\) consumes one positive and one negative discrepancy among children of a depth-\(\ell\) block.  Therefore its total count satisfies
\[
 M_{a,\ell}\le R_{\ell+1}. \tag{15}
\]
Applying the three armwise bijections to the frozen rows gives the original multiplicity of every atom, so the output lies in \(\mathcal S_N(F)\).

All preceding operations are finite and use exact comparisons.  If the input is rational with total bit length \(B\), every nonzero difference between input atoms is at least \(2^{-O(B)}\), while each root length is fixed; hence one may take \(L=O(B)\).  Repeated atoms were aggregated, and a grid contact is handled by the singleton convention.  Thus neither repetitions, small positive rational gaps, nor boundary contacts alter (8), (12), or (15).  This proves the lemma.

Choose an optimal coupling \(\pi^\star\) in Definition def:fractional-value.  The feasible coupling polytope is nonempty and compact because it is a finite-dimensional polytope with fixed empirical margins, so an optimizer exists.  Definition def:rounding-algorithm and Lemma lem:hierarchical-repair produce \(T_{\mathrm{alg}}\in\mathcal S_N(F)\).  Lemma lem:quadratic-slack-accounting gives
\[
 C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)<V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)+\frac{402}{N}. \tag{24}
\]
Every realizable schedule induces a coupling in \(\Gamma(F)\), while \(T_{\mathrm{alg}}\) is feasible in Definition def:realizable-value.  Therefore
\[
 V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)\le V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)
 \le C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)
 <V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)+\frac{402}{N}. \tag{25}
\]
Because \(c_1y_1+c_2y_2+c_3y_3\in[-1/2,1/2]\) on \([0,1]^3\), Definition \(C(y)\) gives \(0\le C(y)\le1/4\).  Combining this trivial range with (25) proves
\[
 0\le V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)
 \le\min\left\{\frac14,\frac{402}{N}\right\}. \tag{26}
\]
The inequality \(402/N<1/4\) is equivalent to \(N>1608\), hence to \(N\ge1609\) for integer \(N\).

We now establish the claimed deterministic bit complexity.  Suppose the rational input has total bit length \(B\).  Aggregating and sorting at most \(N\) atoms per arm is polynomial.  The support \(E\) has at most \(N^3\) cells, and all sets \(G_{as}\) are obtained by scanning this support.  Lemma lem:hierarchical-repair gives a singleton depth \(L=O(B)\).  No grid of size \(2^L\) is materialized: the cell containing a rational endpoint is found by an exact multiplication by \(2^\ell/H_a\) and an integer comparison, so its index has \(O(B)\) bits.

At each depth, the support-elimination argument used to prove (10) implements the basic-table step.  Gaussian elimination over the zero--one incidence matrix produces a rational kernel vector; after clearing denominators it may be chosen integral with coordinates equal to minors of a matrix of order at most \(3N\).  The Leibniz expansion bounds each such minor by \((3N)!\), so every coordinate has \(O(N\log N)\) bits.  Maintain a common denominator \(D\) for the current table.  In an elimination step, \(\varepsilon=q_e/d_e\) for one integral kernel coordinate \(d_e\); after the update, a common denominator is at most \(D|d_e|\).  Thus each elimination adds only \(O(N\log N)\) bits.  There are at most \(N^3\) support eliminations initially and at most polynomially many at each of the \(O(B)\) levels.  Hence all intermediate numerators and denominators have bit length polynomial in \(N+B\), and exact rational arithmetic, Gaussian elimination, and comparison run in polynomial time.

Freezing expands at most \(N\) rows, and the three tree matchings use at most \(O(NL)\) occurrence moves.  Label the output rows by their arm-1 occurrences.  Since every output column has exactly its prescribed occurrence multiset, the arm-2 and arm-3 occurrence labels define two permutations relative to arm 1, including when values repeat.  This proves the algorithmic claim.

For arbitrary real atoms, the finite feasible transportation polytope still has rational vertices because its constraint matrix and integer margins are rational.  A linear objective with real coefficients attains its minimum at some vertex, so an optimal coupling with rational cell masses may be selected.  The finite set of distinct real atoms has positive minimum separation within each arm, and hence some finite singleton depth exists.  The same finite construction and inequalities then prove existence, without making a bit-complexity assertion for real-oracle input.  This completes the proof.

For every \(N\ge4\), Theorem thm:constructive-rounding-upper and Definition def:worst-gap imply
\[
 \Delta_N\le\min\left\{\frac14,\frac{402}{N}\right\}. \tag{27}
\]
The schedule in the already-established Theorem thm:explicit-matching-lower belongs to the same class \([0,1]^{3\times N}\) and has gap \(1/(46080N)\).  Since Definition def:worst-gap takes the supremum over that class,
\[
 \Delta_N\ge\frac1{46080N}. \tag{28}
\]
Both (27) and (28) hold for every integer \(N\ge4\), rather than only on a replication subsequence.  Thus \(r_N=N^{-1}\), \(a=1/46080\), and \(b=402\) give the asserted sharp order and rule out an arithmetic exceptional subsequence for that order.

It remains to prove the exceptional exact assertion at \(N=2\).  Write the two scaled values \(z_{ai}=c_ax_{ai}\) in arm \(a\) as \(m_a-d_a\) and \(m_a+d_a\), where \(d_a\ge0\).  Any coupling can be represented by a law of \(S=(S_1,S_2,S_3)\in\{-1,1\}^3\) with balanced coordinate marginals.  When \(d_a=0\), introduce an independent balanced sign label for the repeated atom; it does not change any value or cost.  Put \(M=\sum_am_a\).  Since \(\mathbb ES_a=0\) for every arm,
\[
 \mathbb E\left(M+\sum_ad_aS_a\right)^2
 =M^2+\mathbb E\left(\sum_ad_aS_a\right)^2. \tag{29}
\]
Replacing the sign law by its antipodal symmetrization preserves every balanced marginal and preserves (29), because the second integrand is even.  Every antipodally symmetric law is a convex combination of the four laws that are uniform on a pair \(\{s,-s\}\).  The objective in (29) is linear in this law, so one of those four pair laws attains its minimum.  That pair law is exactly a two-row schedule: in every arm it uses each of the two marginal occurrences once.  Hence a realizable coupling minimizes whenever a fractional coupling does, and
\[
 V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)=V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)
\]
for every two-row triple.  Taking the supremum proves \(\Delta_2=0\).

Under Assumption ass:complete-randomization, the potential-outcome array is fixed and \(Z\) is the sole source of randomness.  Put
\[
 I_{ai}=\mathbf 1\{Z_i=a\},\qquad Y_{ai}=x_{ai}-\mu_a.
\]
The fixed-count design gives \(\mathbb E I_{ai}=n_a/N\), so
\[
 \mathbb E_Z\widehat\theta_N
 =\sum_ac_an_a^{-1}\sum_i\frac{n_a}{N}x_{ai}
 =\sum_ac_a\mu_a=\theta_N. \tag{30}
\]
For distinct units, direct counting under the same design gives
\[
 \mathbb E(I_{ai}I_{aj})=\frac{n_a(n_a-1)}{N(N-1)},\qquad
 \mathbb E(I_{ai}I_{bj})=\frac{n_an_b}{N(N-1)}\quad(a\ne b), \tag{31}
\]
whereas \(I_{ai}I_{bi}=0\) when \(a\ne b\).  Define
\[
 S_{ab}=\frac1{N-1}\sum_iY_{ai}Y_{bi},\qquad S_a^2=S_{aa}.
\]
Substitution of (31) into the covariance sums, using \(\sum_iY_{ai}=0\), gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z\left(n_a^{-1}\sum_iI_{ai}x_{ai}\right)
 =\left(\frac1{n_a}-\frac1N\right)S_a^2, \tag{32}
\]
and, for \(a\ne b\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_Z\left(n_a^{-1}\sum_iI_{ai}x_{ai},
 n_b^{-1}\sum_iI_{bi}x_{bi}\right)=-\frac{S_{ab}}N. \tag{33}
\]
Let \(\tau_i=\sum_ac_ax_{ai}\) and
\[
 S_\tau^2=\frac1{N-1}\sum_i(\tau_i-\theta_N)^2.
\]
Expanding the variance of the contrast in (32)--(33) yields the finite-population identity
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_N)
 =\sum_a\frac{c_a^2S_a^2}{n_a}-\frac{S_\tau^2}{N}. \tag{34}
\]
If the completion has \(t=N^{-1}\sum_i\tau_i^2\), its fixed marginal moments give
\[
 S_a^2=\frac{N}{N-1}v_a,\quad
 S_\tau^2=\frac{N}{N-1}(t-\theta_N^2). \tag{35}
\]
Using (35) in (34) and the definition of \(B_N(F)\) proves
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_N)
 =\frac{\sum_a(N/n_a)c_a^2v_a+\theta_N^2-t}{N-1}
 =\frac{B_N(F)-t}{N-1}. \tag{36}
\]

Equation (36) is decreasing in \(t\).  Definition def:realizable-value says that the least realizable value is \(V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)\), so Definition def:variance-certificates makes the sharp upper endpoint \(U_N(F)\).  The constructive schedule and the fractional relaxation obey
\[
 V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)\le V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)\le C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F),
\]
and hence
\[
 U_{\mathrm{lo}}(F)\le U_N(F)\le U_{\mathrm{hi}}(F). \tag{37}
\]
Their computable primal--dual width is
\[
 U_{\mathrm{hi}}(F)-U_{\mathrm{lo}}(F)
 =\frac{C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)}{N-1}
 \le\frac{402}{N(N-1)}. \tag{38}
\]
For \(N\ge4\), (38) follows from Theorem thm:constructive-rounding-upper.  Complete randomization into three positive arms also permits \(N=3\); in that case \(0\le C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)\le1/4<402/3\), so (38) still holds.  The already-established Theorem thm:explicit-matching-lower supplies a schedule for which the fractional optimum is not realizable, proving the stated ``need not'' clause.  The conclusion only compares a finite-population \(N\)-row completion with the unrestricted coupling functional; it does not dispute an identified set defined over a superpopulation Fr\'{e}chet class.

For the lower endpoint, expand every empirical arm into \(N\) occurrences and sort the scaled values as \(r_1\le\cdots\le r_N\) and \(s_1\le\cdots\le s_N\).  Any fractional two-coordinate projection can be split among equal-valued occurrences to give a matrix \(P=(P_{ij})\) with nonnegative entries and every row and column sum one.  Write
\[
 s_j=s_1+\sum_{k=1}^{N-1}(s_{k+1}-s_k)\mathbf1\{j>k\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{i,j}P_{ij}r_is_j
 =s_1\sum_ir_i+
 \sum_{k=1}^{N-1}(s_{k+1}-s_k)\sum_i r_iw_{ik},
 \qquad w_{ik}=\sum_{j>k}P_{ij}. \tag{39}
\]
For each \(k\), \(0\le w_{ik}\le1\) and \(\sum_iw_{ik}=N-k\).  An exchange that moves weight from a smaller \(r_i\) to a larger \(r_j\) cannot decrease \(\sum_i r_iw_{ik}\); therefore
\[
 \sum_i r_iw_{ik}\le\sum_{i>k}r_i. \tag{40}
\]
Equations (39)--(40) prove that the equal-rank pairing maximizes the product sum for every fractional pair coupling, with repeats included.

For a three-arm completion, expansion of the total cost gives
\[
 \sum_i\left(\sum_az_{ai}\right)^2
 =\sum_{a,i}z_{ai}^2+2\sum_{a<b}\sum_i z_{ai}z_{bi}. \tag{41}
\]
The one-coordinate square sums in (41) are fixed by the marginals.  Applying (39)--(40) to each pairwise projection bounds every pair-product sum by its comonotone value.  Sorting all three scaled columns increasingly and pairing equal ranks attains all three bounds simultaneously, and is an \(N\)-row realizable schedule.  Hence it attains the maximum cost over both fractional and realizable couplings, namely \(C_{\max}(F)\).  Since (36) decreases with cost, the sharp lower variance endpoint is
\[
 L_N(F)=\frac{B_N(F)-C_{\max}(F)}{N-1}.
\]
This completes the certificate proof.

For a probability law \(H\) on \([0,1]\), let \(Q_H\) be its nondecreasing quantile.  For finite laws, matching equal infinitesimal quantile masses and using
\[
 |r-s|=\int_0^1|\mathbf1\{r\le t\}-\mathbf1\{s\le t\}|\,dt
\]
gives the one-dimensional identity
\[
 W_1(H,K)=\int_0^1|Q_H(u)-Q_K(u)|\,du
 =\int_0^1|H(t)-K(t)|\,dt. \tag{42}
\]
On each interval \(((j-1)/N,j/N]\), monotonicity bounds the integral error from the midpoint quantile value by \(N^{-1}\) times the quantile variation across that interval.  The variations telescope to at most one.  Definition def:plugin-lift and (42) therefore give
\[
 W_1(G_a,\widehat F_a)\le N^{-1}. \tag{43}
\]

Under Assumption ass:complete-randomization, arm \(a\) reveals a simple random sample without replacement of size \(n_a\) from its fixed finite-population column.  For every \(t\in[0,1]\), direct indicator covariance calculation for this hypergeometric count gives
\[
 \mathbb E\widehat F_a(t)=F_a(t),\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat F_a(t))
 =\rho_aF_a(t)\{1-F_a(t)\},\quad
 \rho_a=\frac{N-n_a}{n_a(N-1)}. \tag{44}
\]
Because complete randomization has finite assignment support, expectation is a finite weighted sum; distributing the integral in (42) across that sum, followed pointwise by Cauchy--Schwarz and then by \(p(1-p)\le1/4\), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E W_1(\widehat F_a,F_a)
 &=\int_0^1\mathbb E|\widehat F_a(t)-F_a(t)|\,dt\\
 &\le\sqrt{\rho_a}\int_0^1\sqrt{F_a(t)\{1-F_a(t)\}}\,dt
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\rho_a}. \tag{45}
\end{aligned}
\]
The triangle inequality, (43), and (45) imply
\[
 \mathbb EW_1(G_a,F_a)\le\frac12\sqrt{\rho_a}+N^{-1}. \tag{46}
\]
This argument is armwise and does not assume independence between the observed arms.

We next prove the deterministic perturbation inequalities.  For \(X_a,Y_a\in[0,1]\), both contrasts lie in \([-1/2,1/2]\), so
\[
 \left|\left(\sum_ac_aX_a\right)^2-
 \left(\sum_ac_aY_a\right)^2\right|
 \le\sum_a|c_a|\,|X_a-Y_a|. \tag{47}
\]
Starting from any coupling of \(F\), glue to each coordinate an optimal one-dimensional \(W_1\) transport from \(F_a\) to \(G_a\), conditionally independently given that coordinate.  The resulting triple has marginals \(G\).  Applying (47), then reversing the roles of \(F\) and \(G\), proves
\[
 |V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(G)|
 \le\sum_a|c_a|W_1(F_a,G_a). \tag{48}
\]
The same argument with suprema proves (48) with \(C_{\max}\) in place of \(V_{\mathrm{rel}}\).  Since both \(F\) and \(G\) have \(N\) equal-weight occurrences, sorted coordinatewise matching attains every one-dimensional \(W_1\).  Applying those three bijections to an optimal schedule, and then reversing \(F,G\), gives
\[
 |V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{int}}(G)|
 \le\sum_a|c_a|W_1(F_a,G_a). \tag{49}
\]

For each arm,
\[
 |\mu_a(F)-\mu_a(G)|\le W_1(F_a,G_a). \tag{50}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 v_a(H)=\min_{m\in[0,1]}\int(x-m)^2\,dH(x),
\]
and \(x\mapsto(x-m)^2\) is uniformly \(2\)-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\).  Comparing at the minimizing mean for each law in turn gives
\[
 |v_a(F)-v_a(G)|\le2W_1(F_a,G_a). \tag{51}
\]
Since \(|\theta_N(F)|,|\theta_N(G)|\le1/2\), equation (50) gives
\[
 |\theta_N(F)^2-\theta_N(G)^2|
 \le|\theta_N(F)-\theta_N(G)|
 \le\sum_a|c_a|W_1(F_a,G_a). \tag{52}
\]
Combining (48)--(52) with the definitions of \(B_N\), \(D_N\), and the endpoints yields
\[
 |L_N(G)-L_N(F)|\le\frac{D_N(F,G)}{N-1},\qquad
 |U_N(G)-U_N(F)|\le\frac{D_N(F,G)}{N-1}. \tag{53}
\]
Taking expectations in the definition of \(D_N\) and using (46) proves
\[
 \mathbb ED_N(F,G)\le M_N. \tag{54}
\]

Apply Theorem thm:variance-certificate to \(G\).  Its deterministic width gives
\[
 0\le U_N(G)-U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)\le\frac{402}{N(N-1)},
 \qquad
 0\le U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)-U_N(G)\le\frac{402}{N(N-1)}. \tag{55}
\]
Equations (53) and (55) imply
\[
 \max\{|U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)-U_N(F)|,
 |U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)-U_N(F)|\}
 \le\frac{D_N(F,G)+402/N}{N-1}. \tag{56}
\]

If \(n_a/N\to p_a\in(0,1)\), then \(\rho_a=O(N^{-1})\), the coefficients in \(D_N\) are bounded, and (54) gives \(\mathbb ED_N=O(N^{-1/2})+O(N^{-1})\).  For any nonnegative random variable \(X\) and \(r>0\), the elementary inequality \(\mathbb EX\ge r\,\mathbb P\{X>r\}\) follows by restricting the expectation to \(\{X>r\}\).  Applied to \(D_N\), it gives \(D_N=O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1/2})+O(N^{-1})\).  Dividing (53) and (56) by \(N-1\), and retaining the deterministic term \(402/[N(N-1)]\), proves the asserted \(O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-3/2})+O(N^{-2})\) errors for \(L_N(G)\), \(U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)\), and \(U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)\).

Finally, for \(\eta\in(0,1)\), apply the preceding elementary inequality with \(X=D_N(F,G)\) and \(r=M_N/\eta\).  Equation (54) gives
\[
 \mathbb P\{D_N(F,G)\le M_N/\eta\}\ge1-\eta. \tag{57}
\]
On this event, (56) places \(U_N(F)\) inside
\[
 \left[
 U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)-\frac{M_N/\eta+402/N}{N-1},
 U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)+\frac{M_N/\eta+402/N}{N-1}
 \right].
\]
All quantities in this interval are computable from the observed arm samples, the known arm sizes, the fractional program, and the deterministic rounding output.  This proves the theorem.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Given rational \(F\) and an optimal rational table \(q^\star=N\pi^\star\), aggregate repeated atoms and form the optimal-support slope intervals \(I_{as}\).  For arms \(1,2\), use the root interval \([-1/2,5/4]\), and for arm \(3\), use \([-3/2,0]\).  At depth \(\ell\), divide each arm-specific root into \(D_\ell=2^\ell\) consecutive cells of width \(h_{1,\ell}=h_{2,\ell}=(7/4)2^{-\ell}\) and \(h_{3,\ell}=(3/2)2^{-\ell}\), taking every cell left-closed and right-open except that the last cell is right-closed.  Form \(\mathcal P_{a,\ell}\) by grouping the atom intervals contained in a common cell and declaring every interval not contained in one cell to be a singleton.  From fine to coarse depth, replace the residual table on its current support by a rational basic feasible table with the current integer cluster margins, freeze the integer parts of its cells, and pass the remaining mass upward.  Match the selected and required atoms independently along each partition tree and apply the three resulting bijections to the selected rows.  Output the resulting \(T_{\mathrm{alg}}\in\mathcal S_N(F)\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The original construction used a common length-four grid.  The directed correction uses the exact arm-specific slope roots and widths while leaving freezing, repair, output, and complexity unchanged.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Whether \(\kappa_-=\kappa_+\), the value of a common limit if it exists, and the classification of all asymptotically extremal dual-tight geometries remain open.
open_obligations.obstruction: The handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{exact}}\) supplies neither a proved finite obstruction catalogue nor a compactness theorem preserving normalized slack under block decomposition.  Even after the arm-specific refinement, the cluster-count, residual, and quadratic-charge inequalities are not jointly certified sharp, while the padded four-row witness need not maximize them.
open_obligations.attempted: The ordered slope intervals were compressed into arm-specific nested dyadic blocks, residual tables were sparsified and repaired exactly, and the four-row zero-slack face was solved over the reals and integers.  The sharper accounting closes the uniform rate with constant 402 but still provides no matching constant-level variational principle or exclusion of larger irreducible blocks.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved frontier gives the sharper compact localization
\[
 \frac1{46080}\le \kappa_-\le\kappa_+\le402.
\]
The lower endpoint is witnessed for every \(N\ge4\) by one fixed four-row obstruction padded with isolated dummy rows, while the arm-specific ordered-support multiscale repair supplies the upper endpoint.  Thus the \(N^{-1}\) order and the absence of an arithmetic exceptional subsequence are settled.  What remains unresolved is equality of the two asymptotic constants, the value of a common constant if it exists, and the classification of all extremal obstruction geometries.

prose_updates.tldr: Fractional multi-marginal transport can produce a sharper-looking three-arm variance bound than any \(N\)-unit potential-outcome table can realize.  For the bounded scalar contrast \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\), the worst same-empirical-marginal discrepancy is exactly of order \(N^{-1}\): arm-specific optimal-support slope grids, basic-table freezing, and hierarchical repair give a deterministic bit-polynomial schedule with loss less than \(402/N\), while an explicit four-row obstruction padded by isolated dummy rows loses exactly \(1/(46080N)\) for every \(N\ge4\).  Under complete randomization this finite-population operational correction becomes a computable \(O(N^{-2})\) band around the sharp upper variance endpoint, without contradicting Gao--Ge--Qian's superpopulation identified-set theorem.  Armwise empirical quantile lifts consistently estimate both variance endpoints while retaining the larger sampling-without-replacement error as a separate term.

project_justification.gap: Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) identify superpopulation causal variance bounds over fractional multi-marginal couplings, whereas a fixed population of \(N\) units requires one common \(N\)-row schedule; the distinction is operational and is not a contradiction of their theorem.  Emami and Pass (2025) demonstrate discrete non-Monge optimality and request quantitative error bounds in a different quadratic orientation.  Haus (2015) treats exact mixability and bottleneck approximation, and Brennan et al. (2025) rely on integer programming without an analytic realization width.
project_justification.niche: The unfilled object is the worst additive loss between a fractional optimum and an \(N\)-row optimum for the same three scalar \([0,1]\) empirical marginals and the fixed contrast \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\), together with an exact-rational construction polynomial in the input bit length.  The lower obstruction embeds into broader quadratic multi-marginal transport classes with \(K\ge3\) and \(d\ge1\), but the upper theorem is deliberately confined to this \(K=3,d=1\) class.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact arm-specific ordered dual-slope ranges, a multiscale exact-marginal repair algorithm with loss less than \(402/N\), an all-\(N\ge4\) rational lower family, and design-based endpoint certificates with explicit sampling-without-replacement plug-in error.

prose_updates.related_work: Emami and Pass (2025, Introduction, Example 1, and Discussion) move from the empirical Kantorovich relaxation to Monge implementability, prove a minimal non-Monge quadratic example, and identify quantitative approximation error as future work; their barycenter cost has the opposite squared-sum orientation from the signed scalar contrast here.  Friesecke (2019, Theorem 2.2 and Section 3) analyzes non-Monge extreme points in a symmetric finite transport polytope but gives no all-denominator additive rate.  Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1) identify a superpopulation causal bound with fractional multi-marginal transport and prove plug-in rates; Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}variance\mbox{-}certificate}\) instead quantifies the operational error incurred when the same empirical marginals must be realized by one \(N\)-row fixed-population schedule, so the results are complementary rather than contradictory.  Haus (2015, Theorem 3 and the approximation section) proves hardness of exact matrix mixability and a bottleneck approximation result, objectives that do not subsume additive average squared-contrast rounding.  Altschuler and Boix-Adser\`a (2023, Algorithm 3) restore exact marginals after approximate tensor optimization but remain inside the fractional transportation polytope.  Puccetti and Wang (2015, Theorem 1.1 and Section 5) give the rearrangement representation and document unresolved higher-dimensional negative-dependence geometry; their discretization comparison changes the marginals rather than imposing same-\(N\) row realizability.  Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Lemma 1 and equations (7)--(11)) give sharp two-arm variance endpoints, recovered exactly by \(\mathrm{prop{:}two\mbox{-}arm\mbox{-}reduction}\).  Brennan et al. (2025, Sections 2--3) compute finite completions for general designs by integer programming and motivate an analytic certificate in the present restricted geometry.  Li and Ding (2017, Theorems 3--4) supply the fixed-potential-outcome complete-randomization framework, while Hammer et al. (1996) provide a concrete multi-arm trial consumer.  Adding zero coordinates and zero-coefficient arms embeds the lower obstruction into the broader \(K\ge3,d\ge1\) quadratic transport setting, but the \(O(N^{-1})\) achievability proof uses the note's exact \(K=3,d=1,[0,1]\) fixed-contrast geometry and does not transfer to arbitrary \(K,d\), or quadratic form \(A\).
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The improved universal constant \(402\) remains deliberately loose: \(402/N\) becomes strictly smaller than the trivial cost-gap bound \(1/4\) only at \(N=1609\), so the useful numerical report at ordinary trial sizes is the actual primal--dual width \([C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)]/(N-1)\).  The exact large-\(N\) constant remains open within \([1/46080,402]\), as does the extremal geometry.  The plug-in uncertainty band uses a first-moment Markov argument rather than a nonsmooth transport limit law, so sampling error dominates deterministic rounding error under proportional allocation.  Finally, only the lower obstruction automatically embeds into broader \(K\ge3,d\ge1\) quadratic transport classes; the achievability proof is specific to three scalar arms on \([0,1]\) and the fixed contrast.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note proves the sharp \(N^{-1}\) order, the explicit constants \(1/46080\) and \(402\), the all-\(N\ge4\) lower family, the rational bit-polynomial algorithm, the finite-population variance translation, and the plug-in endpoint bounds.  It is an operational correction for realizing a fractional functional on one fixed \(N\)-unit science table, not a contradiction of a superpopulation identified-set result.  The lower obstruction extends to broader quadratic multi-marginal classes by adding zero coordinates and zero-coefficient arms, but the upper rate is proved only for \(K=3,d=1,[0,1]\) and \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\).  The theorem does not assert that one experiment observes all three full marginals, that every interior variance in the interval hull is attained, or that the unknown actual completion has variance at least \(U_{\mathrm{lo}}(F)\).  The exact value of \(\Delta_3\) and the limit of \(N\Delta_N\) remain outside the proved result; the two-row realization loss is exactly zero.
